note: Human rulings on obligations the rubric does not determine. A ruled obligation is neither a match nor a miss: it is reported as its own category so a genuinely undecidable case is never silently counted as either. Rulings are frozen; add entries, do not edit them.

policy.denominator: Ambiguous obligations stay in the obligation denominator and are reported separately. They are NOT excluded, because excluding them would inflate recall by removing the hardest cases.
policy.obligation_status: An obligation is `hit` if it issue-matches and is not ruled ambiguous; `ambiguous` if ruled ambiguous and it issue-matched; `miss` otherwise. A ruled obligation with no issue-match is still a miss — the ruling governs how a match is counted, not whether one occurred.
policy.escalation: A judge-emitted `ambiguous` verdict is the natural next rubric revision, but it changes the rubric and so requires re-baselining. Until then ambiguity is curated here.

rulings.gold_claim: In `coveringNumber_le_packingNumber`, replace the manual `by_cases` proof with the `by_cases!` pattern and use `encard_maximalSeparatedSet` together with `IsCover.coveringNumber_le_encard`.
rulings.rationale: Candidates ask to rename `card_maximalSeparatedSet` to `encard_maximalSeparatedSet` and update downstream uses. Because the gold ask's own text names the renamed form, the requested proof rewrite presupposes the rename — the candidate requests a prerequisite of the maintainer's change rather than the change itself. Whether a prerequisite counts as the same issue is not settled by the rubric: 'a different fix may still issue-match' points one way, 'a rename when the ask is a proof change is false' points the other. Both v7.1 and v8 returned issue=True 3/3 on this pair, with reasoning that is defensible either way, so it is not judge noise.

candidates_for_ruling.gold_claim: In `coveringNumber_two_mul_le_externalCoveringNumber`, replace the `rcases Set.eq_empty_or_nonempty A` split with `(rfl | h_nonempty)` and discharge the empty case by `simp`.
candidates_for_ruling.why: Candidates argue the split is dead code because `h_nonempty` is unused and propose removing it. Same rubric tension as the ruled entry, and the judge split its own samples 2-of-3 on it under v7.1 — the empirical signature of ambiguity. Not ruled: awaiting a human decision.
